newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurocopter sees Tiger contract signed June 20.
newsitem.headline: Eurocopter sees Tiger contract signed June 20.

text.p: Franco-German venture Eurocopter expects to sign a contract for setting up production lines for its Tiger combat helicopter on June 20, Eurocopter chairman Jean-Francois Bigay said on Saturday.

He told Reuters at the Paris air show that the new Socialist defence minister, Alain Richard, had told him the contract would be signed next Friday. Richard was accompanying President Jacques Chirac on the official opening ceremony for the show.
"I saw Mr Richard this morning during the visit. He confirmed to me that the production investment will be signed June 20," he said in an interview.
Eurocopter is 70 percent owned by French state-owned Aerospatiale and 30 percent by Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG of Germany.

France is ordering 80 ground support versions and Germany is buying the same number of anti-tank helicopters. The French order is estimated at 12 billion francs, after a 10 percent price cut demanded by the DGA French procurement agency, he said.
The first deliveries are expected in 2002-2003.
